name: Sewer socialism
summary: Sewer socialism was the pragmatic, reformist socialism of Milwaukee's Social-Democrats from the 1890s to 1960. It held that socialists should win city hall and show that honest, efficient, publicly owned services such as water, sanitation, power, parks and schools improve workers' lives, building toward socialism by steady change. It was allied with trade unions, hostile to revolutionary phrasing and to Bolshevism, and opposed to U.S. entry into the First World War.
scope: The Milwaukee strand of the Socialist Party of America, represented by Victor Berger, Emil Seidel and Daniel Hoan, with reference to Berger's 1906 and 1921 writings, from about 1897 to the 1930s. It excludes later Zeidler-era liberalism, modern revivals such as New York's 'pothole politics', and the broader democratic socialism audited separately. Many modern-issue statements are low-confidence inferences.

keyFigures.name: Victor L. Berger
keyFigures.role: Founder and chief theorist of Milwaukee socialism and the first Socialist elected to Congress.

keyFigures.name: Emil Seidel
keyFigures.role: First Socialist mayor of a major U.S. city, elected in Milwaukee in 1910.

keyFigures.name: Daniel Hoan
keyFigures.role: Milwaukee mayor from 1916 to 1940, who made the city a model of honest Socialist administration.

sources.title: Milwaukee Sewer Socialism

sources.usedFor: Labor alliance of 1897, municipal services, rejection of Progressive regulation, anti-graft focus and Berger's wartime prosecution.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Berger's program aimed to strengthen working people physically as well as economically, and Hoan's Milwaukee expanded health inspections and vaccinations; national health provision is a natural extension but is not documented.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Never addressed as a minimum wage; inferred from the program of policies favoring working people such as the eight-hour day and lifting workers out of extreme poverty.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Socialists who wanted public ownership of utilities and monopolies did not trust unregulated markets, though sewer socialists were pragmatic and not hostile to all private business.

public-ownership.rationale: Municipal ownership of water, power and street railways was the movement's signature program, and Hoan pressed for city ownership of the electric utility and streetcars.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Hoan judged government by services delivered rather than low taxes; progressive taxation to fund them is inferred, not documented in the sources opened.

unions-good.rationale: Berger credits Socialists with always introducing bills to protect labor, and the Social-Democrats were founded in 1897 as an alliance with Milwaukee's trade unions.

property-fundamental.rationale: A socialist movement seeking public ownership of utilities and monopolies treats private property as overridable for public purposes, though it did not seek confiscation of personal property.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Historians report that Milwaukee Socialists rejected the Progressive idea of regulating industry in favor of public ownership and honest government, so adherents are split between favoring tighter rules and preferring ownership.

cut-welfare.rationale: Socialists sought to rescue workers from extreme poverty and fought for labor and social protection bills, so cutting welfare runs against their program.

worker-ownership.rationale: Sewer socialists stressed public rather than worker-owned enterprises; the cooperative commonwealth was a distant aim Berger declined to describe.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Inferred from Berger's condemnation of wartime government suppression of Socialists; no source addresses terrorism surveillance.

legalize-drugs.rationale: The movement never addressed drug policy and adherents have no distinctive stance.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Inferred from Socialists' own experience of Espionage Act persecution making them wary of speech restrictions; not addressed directly.

strong-leader.rationale: The movement valued honest, incorruptible, accountable legislators and the ballot; a leader bypassing gridlock cuts against its democratic party politics.

state-harmful.rationale: Sewer socialists built their program on active, honest government providing services, and Berger demanded reforms within the existing state.

limit-guns.rationale: Berger in 1906 argued for systematically arming all the people since an armed people is free, which suggests opposition to strict limits; inferred.

empower-police-military.rationale: Hoan professionalised police with a merit system and better pay, but the movement opposed militarism; the answer is inferred and mixed.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: The sources never address it and adherents of the era were not distinctive on it.

decide-locally.rationale: Municipal socialism placed the strongest reform capacity in city government, though Berger also pursued national office and national reforms such as pensions.

rehabilitation.rationale: Reform-minded municipal socialists favored professionalised police and public health approaches; the prison stance is inferred.

traditional-family.rationale: Inferred from a progressive reform movement that backed women's suffrage and child welfare; no direct statement on the family.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: An anachronistic question the movement never faced, with no basis to infer a stance.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed in the sources and an anachronistic issue for the era.

more-religion-public.rationale: Berger mocked belief in heavens ancient, Christian or Socialist and joined the secular, Turner-influenced milieu, so a larger public role for religion is unlikely.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Sources show a split: Berger held ugly views on race while later Socialist mayors like Zeidler pushed integrated housing.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The question was not posed in the movement's era and nothing can be inferred.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Berger criticised patriotism and commercialism but also defended German-Americans against wartime hatred; split and not documented.

gradual-change.rationale: Berger insisted on steady change one step at a time, but he valued reform of institutions via the ballot rather than reverence for the established order.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Berger was himself an immigrant and condemned nativist hatred of ethnic groups in 1921, yet restrictionism was common among AFL-aligned socialists of the time; not documented here.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The UN postdates the movement; Berger's antimilitarism suggests sympathy for peace bodies but this is not documented.

free-trade.rationale: No source states a view, and socialists of the era were split.

nation-first.rationale: Berger rejected patriotism and imperialism as inherited prejudices, so an adherent resists putting national interest first.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Inferred from the movement's opposition to US entry into World War I and to imperialism.

open-borders.rationale: Berger's anti-nativism is documented but he is not known to have backed open borders; inferred.

limit-growth.rationale: The movement was pro-development and constructive about industrial civilization; inferred.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic issue; the movement's conservation work is limited to parks and sanitation.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Not addressed, though the sanitary engineering optimism of the movement leans modestly positive.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Nuclear power postdates the movement and its sources never touch energy beyond city-run power plants, so there is no basis for a stance.

revolution-justified.rationale: Berger denounced revolutionary phrases and sought change by ballot, though he conceded evolution does not rule out bloody revolutions in principle.

experts-over-public.rationale: Hoan's merit system and efficiency orientation lean technocratic, but the movement also stressed popular vote; split.

central-planning.rationale: Berger said little was known about the cooperative commonwealth and focused on piecemeal public ownership, not comprehensive central planning.

socialized-markets.rationale: Municipal enterprises coexisted with private markets in Milwaukee, so a mixed arrangement is acceptable; inferred.

land-value-tax.rationale: Berger complained about Single Taxers in 1921 as non-Socialist allies; no stance on a land tax.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from a general redistributive program; not documented.

basic-income.rationale: An unconditional state income was not part of the movement's program of public works, union protections and municipal services, and no source mentions it.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The sources opened give no view on tariffs, and socialists of the era split between protection and free trade.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Hoan used city enterprise and amortization fund management but no strategic investment policy is documented.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Socialists sought collective ownership of monopolies, not distributed small property, though they allied with farmers.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Berger said little is known of the cooperative commonwealth and focused on near-term reforms, so abolishing money and wages is no program.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: No documented stance; a market-money abolition is alien to the movement.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Berger favored independent unions and the AFL, not state-recognised bodies setting wages.

one-party-rule.rationale: Berger in 1921 rejected sect-like exclusivism and Bolshevism, spoke of politics as compromise with majority will, and ran for office in a competitive electoral system.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: A democratic republican movement; the question is not addressed but hereditary rule is contrary to its principles.

democracy-best.rationale: Politics as compromise abiding by the will of the majority was Berger's stated principle, and the movement won power by elections.

direct-votes.rationale: Early American socialists generally backed initiative and referendum, but the sources opened do not say so for Milwaukee.

workers-councils.rationale: Berger opposed the Russian-style revolution and parliament-free politics, preferring elected office.

right-to-secede.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from national political reform orientation.

natural-rulers.rationale: Berger blasted plutocracy and favored representation of wage-working class; belief in natural rulers contradicts it.

political-violence-never.rationale: Berger said the evolutionary view does not exclude bloody revolution but his movement acted nonviolently; adherents are split.

war-builds-character.rationale: Berger called World War the greatest triumph of darkness and reaction and was prosecuted for opposing it.

separate-church-state.rationale: Berger's secular outlook and Turner associations suggest strict separation, though not a documented plank in the opened sources.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Berger's mocking of religious heavens and the secular character of the program make scripture-based law implausible.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Socialists wanted public provision of services including justice; private provision conflicts with the program.

military-superiority.rationale: Berger criticised patriotism, imperialism and commercialism and opposed US intervention in the war.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Berger condemned racial and national hatreds in 1921 and the party published in multiple languages to reach immigrant voters.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Berger described himself as evolutionary and put weight on class alliance with progressive farmers; Marxist class-struggle theory was downplayed by sewer socialists.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The program stressed lifting workers from poverty, not full equality of outcomes; split.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: The movement's sources never discuss Indigenous peoples or land rights, so no position can be inferred.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Anti-imperialist but nothing about reparations in the sources.

civilizational-union.rationale: Inferred from Berger's critique of patriotism and nationalism.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Socialists urged collective provision and constructive public work over private gain.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Berger defended civil liberties against wartime suppression, suggesting rights are not subordinated to duties; inferred.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: The movement created parks and beaches for people, but intrinsic value of nature was not discussed.

limit-population.rationale: Berger's eugenicist leanings noted in PBS Wisconsin hint at sympathy but sources are thin.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The movement aimed to clean up the legacy of industrialisation through sanitation and public works, not reject industrial civilisation.

accelerate-technology.rationale: No source gives a view on speeding technological disruption; the movement's engineering optimism was about sanitation and utilities, not disruption.

human-enhancement.rationale: Bodily enhancement technology is far outside the movement's period and sources, so no stance can be inferred.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anachronistic; its emphasis on honest elected officials makes it unlikely.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Encryption is anachronistic for a movement of the early twentieth century and the sources say nothing on it.

restore-past-order.rationale: Berger said we want to be constructive and build up, with a progressive orientation, not restore a lost order.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Sewer socialism is defined as the pragmatic emphasis on honest, efficient public works over ideological dispute, and Berger scorned revolutionary phrases for concrete achievements.

direct-action.rationale: Berger denounced IWW-style revolutionary phrases and insisted on a political party working through elections and a working program.

means-match-ends.rationale: Berger worried socialists might simply change masters and wanted constructive means, but no explicit principle is stated.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Sewer socialism sought to clean up and improve industrial cities with sanitation and public works, which contradicts abandoning civilization.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: The movement valued efficient professional administration and public services; no such aim.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Berger said little can be said about the cooperative commonwealth, so the distribution principle was left open.

production-for-use.rationale: Public ownership of utilities served community needs rather than profit, a core municipal-socialist rationale.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Berger focused on strengthening workers and reforms rather than expounding surplus-value theory.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Berger rejected Russian-style bloody revolution and Communist ideas as despairing of the ballot.

collective-farming.rationale: Berger sought a class alliance with farmers of progressive views, implying support for individual farmers; inferred.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Berger linked the war with commercialism, patriotism and imperialism and blamed the capitalist plutocracy for it.

taxation-theft.rationale: Hoan judged government by services delivered, not low taxes, reflecting the movement's view of taxation as the legitimate price of public goods.

harm-principle.rationale: No source states a general theory of limits on state power; the movement reasoned from public health and welfare, not Mill's principle.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The sources do not address individual versus group rights, and a labor movement built on collective organisation gives no clear lean.

conscription.rationale: Berger opposed US entry into World War I and was prosecuted for it, but Hoan ran draft registration as mayor, so adherents were split in practice.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Voting and political participation were the movement's strategy.

state-as-business.rationale: Hoan's amortization fund and business-like efficiency fit, but citizens as customers conflicts with public ownership; split.

positive-liberty.rationale: Berger wanted workers economically, morally and physically strengthened so they could resist, which expresses a material view of freedom.

media-academia-power.rationale: Berger built his movement on a daily press but did not make this claim.

hereditarian-race.rationale: PBS Wisconsin reports that Berger held eugenicist and ugly racial views, though the movement as a whole was progressive; contested among adherents.

organic-representation.rationale: Representation through families and trade bodies is not in any source; the movement worked through ordinary elections to councils and legislatures.

total-state.rationale: Berger rejected dogma and sectarian control and sought limited constructive reforms.

national-rebirth.rationale: Berger argued for steady, constructive change, not a radical national rebirth from decadence, and the sources never use that frame.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Berger condemned imperialism among inherited prejudices, so the movement rejects expansion of a nation's territory abroad.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Authority resting on personal oaths conflicts with a movement that won office by votes and prized incorruptible public officers.

bound-labor.rationale: Binding farm workers to land with labor duties contradicts the movement's labor-protection program and the farmer alliance Berger wanted.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: The sources show no epistemological stance; the movement's appeal was to honest, efficient administration judged by results.

universal-morality.rationale: No source addresses moral universalism, and the movement's sources are purely political and practical.

single-common-good.rationale: Berger embraced politics as compromise among interests, suggesting rejection, yet public good rhetoric was common; split.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Berger was of Jewish descent and noted wartime suffering of Jews, but his stance on a Jewish state is not documented.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Neither the movement nor Berger addressed diaspora return rights in the sources opened.

revive-national-language.rationale: Nothing in the sources concerns language revival; the movement's press ran in several immigrant languages.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Public ownership was the model; democratic votes in firms are not documented for the movement.

school-vouchers.rationale: The movement created public higher education and favored public schools.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Hoan built an amortization fund to make the city debt-free and was proud of fiscal solvency, though that was municipal, not macroeconomic policy.

economic-freedom.rationale: Berger argued capitalism leaves workers weak and needing economic strengthening to be free.

rule-by-example.rationale: Movement relied on laws, programs and elections; honest example mattered, but not in place of laws.

national-self-determination.rationale: Berger lamented national hatreds and wartime persecution of Germans, Irish, Jews; inferred support for self-determination.

force-without-un.rationale: Berger opposed US entry into the First World War, which implies reluctance to use force abroad; the UN postdates him, so this is inferred.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Berger's skeptical remarks about heavens and scientific Socialism show a rationalist outlook, but this is not elaborated.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Berger condemned immigrant hatred and favored workers' protections regardless of origin; inferred.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Hoan's work programs and public employment are suggestive but the stance is not documented.

class-collaboration.rationale: Berger sought alliance with progressive farmers but represented the wage-working class and rejected the notion that a program compromises it; employers as partners is not his view.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The movement built libraries, parks and public colleges and would not sacrifice cultural institutions to a political goal.

dominated-front.rationale: A bloc of countries dominated by Western powers was not part of the movement's concerns, and no source mentions it.

workers-nation.rationale: Berger criticised patriotism and nationalism and the party had an internationalist outlook.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Inferred from a progressive municipal reform platform; the sources opened say nothing on gender roles.

ban-interest.rationale: Not part of any program; movement was pragmatic about finance.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Frank Zeidler pushed integrated housing, and the movement opposed legalised segregation despite Berger's own racial views.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Berger used the state as a tool for reform and said politics runs on majority will; the instrumental Marxist theory was downplayed.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Fossil fuel production is not addressed; the movement dealt with city-owned utilities rather than energy supply policy.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Berger defended immigrants against prejudice but is not documented on assimilation.

elite-replacement.rationale: Berger condemned racial and national hatreds; conspiratorial claims are alien to him.

proportional-representation.rationale: Early American socialists generally supported proportional representation, but no source opened states it for this movement.

national-mission.rationale: Berger condemned imperialism and patriotism as inherited prejudice.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The sources opened do not discuss structural sexism, so no stance can be derived.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Berger called other parties uncertain and often dishonest and the government a plutocracy; the movement's reputation was built on rooting out graft.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: PBS Wisconsin cites Berger's eugenicist tendency, but the movement was not generally eugenicist; contested.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Berger condemned the persecution and terror against Socialists; accountability is inferred.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Sewer socialism is defined by an active municipality running sanitation, water, power, parks and schools, the opposite of a minimal state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Reported ugly racial views of Berger conflict with the general progressive stance; inferred as split.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Berger deplored the persecution of Jews, Irish, Black Americans and immigrants and the movement stood for equal rights, though Berger's own record is mixed.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Not addressed; Berger favored an American road via the ballot.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: No source covers settler colonialism, though Berger's anti-imperialism points mildly toward disapproval.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: The sources do not discuss religious personal law, which was not an American issue in this period.

restrict-conversion.rationale: A secular, reformist movement with a pluralist immigrant base would not back legal limits on religious conversion.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Banning cattle slaughter is foreign to the movement, which focused on public health through inspection rather than prohibition.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Berger's scorn for heavens of every kind suggests secular public schools, though the sources do not state a school policy.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Berger opposed Communist ideas; the question is about Soviet-style states.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Berger said politics means abiding by the will of the majority.

trade-surplus.rationale: The sources give no view on export surpluses or mercantilism.

population-transfer.rationale: Berger condemned national and racial hatreds, so a government pressuring a minority to leave contradicts his stated outlook.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Berger said evolution does not exclude bloody revolutions yet his movement acted through the ballot, so adherents are split on an absolute rule.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Constructive collective building was the movement's emphasis.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Berger was himself persecuted by wartime government and opposed such suppression.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Berger wanted workers rescued from poverty to resist; inferred.

separated-powers.rationale: The sources never address checks and balances, which the movement did not make a theme.

vanguard-party.rationale: Berger rejected the Communists and sectarian ironclad rules, wanting a broad party that wins elections.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Berger's first duty was to strengthen workers and rescue people from extreme poverty.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Hoan's Garden Homes cooperative housing was a public venture; sale rights are not documented.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Berger credits Socialists with fighting for bills protecting labor.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Berger blamed the capitalist system and aimed at economic reform, which rejects a Malthusian explanation of poverty.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Berger discussed multiplicity of races as an obstacle to organising but condemned prejudice rather than endorsing the claim.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Sewer socialists won office by elections and prized honest representatives, so choosing officials by lot has no place in the program.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Berger denounced the Wilson administration's suppression during the war.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Hoan ran municipal food markets in wartime as demonstration of Socialist business principles.

party-controls-media.rationale: Berger ran daily newspapers and was prosecuted for his editorials, so government or party control of the press contradicts his experience.

party-commands-army.rationale: Berger criticised militarism and relied on parliamentary politics, which excludes party command of armed forces.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: The sources give no naturalisation policy; Berger's immigrant origins argue against long waits but nothing is documented.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Socialist officials often took workers' wages as an ethos; not documented in these sources.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Berger attacked rigid, ironclad party rules inherited from the Socialist Labor Party, yet the Milwaukee organization was highly disciplined; split.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Not addressed, and the European Union postdates the movement.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Berger distrusted executive war power as shown by his critique of the Wilson administration; inferred.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is outside the movement's concerns and the sources say nothing about it.

clerical-rule.rationale: A secular democratic movement that mocked religious heavens.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Berger opposed US entry into the war and was prosecuted, while Hoan cooperated with draft registration; adherents were split on resisting their own government.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Berger was prosecuted under the Espionage Act for his editorials and condemned wartime suppression of ideas, so censorship of art on moral grounds is unlikely to appeal; inferred.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Hoan won election repeatedly from 1916 to 1940, but term limits are not addressed.

recall-officials.rationale: Inferred from early socialist support for popular control of officials; not documented in the sources opened.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Berger's anti-imperialist, antiwar outlook suggests it; inferred.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Hoan's Garden Homes was cooperative rather than ownership-only and the movement did not seek to end renting.

people-in-arms.rationale: Berger wrote in 1906 that evolutionary socialists wanted a systematic way of arming all the people, citing Switzerland, because an armed people is free and strong.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The movement was urban and its base was city workers; inferred.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: The movement's sources do not address partition or reunification.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The movement was led by teachers and professionals like Berger and built public colleges.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Berger's reported racial views conflict with the progressive majority; split.

death-penalty.rationale: Not documented; reform-minded socialists of the era generally opposed it, so inferred.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Not addressed; school health programs existed such as medical exams for children but not sex education.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Berger's rationalist and secular outlook, with Turner influence on the movement, opposes teaching creationism in public schools; inferred.

restrict-pornography.rationale: The sources do not discuss obscenity law; Berger's own press suffered censorship, which makes adherents cautious but not clearly opposed.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Berger was an immigrant and condemned hatred of other nationals; inferred.

minority-language-support.rationale: Milwaukee Socialists published papers in several languages to reach immigrant voters, which suggests sympathy with minority-language public services; inferred.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Exemptions from general law for religious minorities are not mentioned in any source opened.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: The sources never consider social conformity or Mill's argument, so no position is documented.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: International debt was not a theme for a municipal and national reform movement in this period.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Colonial independence is not discussed in the sources, so the movement gives no clear stance.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Rewriting a constitution by assembly was not part of the movement's reform program, which worked within existing city and state institutions.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Berger valued the ballot and suffered wartime suppression, so trading political freedom for growth contradicts his outlook.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Foreign aid is not discussed, and the movement focused on local conditions, so no position is documented.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear weapons postdate Berger, but his antimilitarism points against independent deterrents; inferred.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The sources do not address executive selection, though Berger favored democratic election in general.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Monetary institutions are not discussed in any source opened.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Berger's anti-nationalism and antiwar stance suggest land is not worth fighting for, but no source speaks to territorial compromise.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Berger's program aimed to strengthen workers and socialise monopolies, treating property rights as bounded by public need.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Berger rejected Russian Bolshevism and its bloody revolution, but the sources do not give his analysis of the Soviet economy.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental precaution is anachronistic, though the movement's sanitation work was preventive public health.

collective-defense.rationale: Berger opposed US entry into the First World War and alliance logic that drags nations into war, so he would reject automatic collective defense; inferred.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: The sources contain nothing on annexation and occupation law.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Berger mocked religion but the sources show no program to curb church property, so the movement is unclear on state control of churches.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Ceremonial heads of state are not discussed; a party movement like this had no stance.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: The sources do not discuss secession, though antiwar sympathies lean against using force.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Regional autonomy arrangements are not discussed in the sources opened.

sacred-ruler.rationale: A secular, democratic, anti-hereditary movement rejects the idea of a sacred or divine head of state.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Hoan judged government by services not low tax rates; progressive taxation inferred.

character-from-environment.rationale: Socialist reform programs of sanitation and education assume circumstances shape people; Berger wanted working people strengthened by environment.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Berger criticised government lawlessness in wartime and valued honest government.

space-expansion.rationale: Space expansion is anachronistic and not mentioned in sources.

mixed-constitution.rationale: The sources do not address constitutional theory in the classical sense.

leader-cult.rationale: The movement stressed incorruptible service, not personality cults.

equal-parenting.rationale: Child custody law is not discussed in the sources opened.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: The movement never theorised life under socialism; Berger said little is known about the cooperative commonwealth.

land-redistribution.rationale: Berger allied with farmers rather than seizing estates; inferred.

refugee-return.rationale: The sources do not discuss refugees' return after conflict.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Berger condemned national hatreds and imperialism, which excludes claiming territory because co-nationals live there.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Punishing departure from a religion contradicts the secular, rationalist outlook of Berger and the movement.

women-must-cover.rationale: Dress mandates for women have no place in a progressive, secular reform movement.

common-currency.rationale: Currency unions are not discussed in the sources opened.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Berger criticised nationalism and national prejudices, so unions of kin peoples have no appeal; inferred.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Multilingual party press suggests sympathy, but cultural autonomy is not documented.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Berger's own career shows an immigrant integrating into American politics; inferred.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Berger cited economic conditions as a precondition but stressed education and moral strengthening alongside, so adherents did not hold a strict materialist theory.

ban-cartels.rationale: Socialists wanted trusts and monopolies publicly owned; breaking them up was the Progressive rather than socialist remedy, so only partly agreed.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bank bailouts are not discussed; the movement stressed public ownership of utilities, not rescue of failing firms.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Berger accepted majority will but suffered from state suppression; split.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: The sources give no view on quotas for public bodies.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: A shut-off colonial bloc contradicts Berger's anti-imperialism and the internationalism of the Socialist Party.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Trade agreements are not discussed, but the movement's labor-protection emphasis suggests support for binding labor standards; inferred.

moral-incentives.rationale: Replacing material incentives is not a stated aim, since Berger left the cooperative commonwealth undefined.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Berger denounced impotent revolutionary phrases and said a prerequisite of socialism is strengthening the proletariat and allies, not putschism.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: A democratic labor movement opposing plutocracy and privilege would abolish titles, though the sources never name this specifically.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Berger criticised school teaching of patriotism and inherited prejudice, but no source states a view on how history should be centred, so the answer is split.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Berger condemned imperialism as an inherited prejudice taught alongside patriotism and commercialism, which excludes rule over other peoples as tutelage.

patriotic-education.rationale: Berger said schools taught patriotism and imperialism as inherited prejudices, so adherents would resist loyalty drills in schools; inferred from that remark.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Racial preference in admissions is anachronistic, and the movement's record is mixed between Berger's reported racial views and Zeidler's integration efforts.

public-money-creation.rationale: Money creation is not addressed in any source opened.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Berger believed a great deal could be done under capitalism and that it would grow into socialism by steady change, not collapse.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Berger condemned imperialism, so cultivating influence in former colonies is contrary to his stance.

delink-world-market.rationale: Dependency theory postdates the movement and the sources say nothing on delinking.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: The sources do not discuss exploitation of the global periphery by rich-country workers.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Opposed to economic privilege and the movement's equality stance; inferred, as private discrimination law is not discussed.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The sources do not discuss constitutional rights entrenchment, so there is no documented position.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Colonial treaties are not discussed in the sources opened.

elective-rulers.rationale: A movement winning office through elections and opposed to privilege favors electing rulers over heredity.

minority-veto.rationale: Berger said politics means abiding by the will of the majority.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Berger condemned the lawlessness of the Wilson administration; inferred.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Parliament versus monarchy is not a US issue and sources say nothing, though Berger's majority-rule view favors legislatures.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal welfare is not covered in the sources opened.

animal-use-humane.rationale: The sources do not discuss animal use, though meat inspection was part of municipal sanitation in the era.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Socialists wanted rights and public provision, not charitable duty of the rich.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The movement is defined by active politics and officeholding.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Berger argued school, church and business taught inherited prejudices, but this is thin; split.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Berger noted prejudices taught by school, church, business and society, a partial fit; thin.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: The sources do not discuss global inequality theory; Berger's concern was domestic capitalist plutocracy.

native-born-offices.rationale: Berger, an Austrian-born immigrant elected to Congress, shows the movement would reject reserving offices for the native-born.

party-own-road.rationale: Berger insisted on conditions of the particular country and rejected Russian-pattern revolution, implying each party takes its own road.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Development strategy for poor countries is not discussed in the sources.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Berger's critique of patriotism and imperialism opposes demanding lost land back.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Political leadership by descendants of pre-colonial peoples is not discussed in the sources.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: The movement predates fascism's rise; anti-fascism of later socialists suggests agreement but thin.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Berger opposed Bolshevism but also the Wilson government's repression; split.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: The sources opened do not discuss this; the movement's progressive outlook would reject the denial of slavery as the main cause.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Monuments debates are not covered in any source opened.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Not covered in any source; the issue is anachronistic for the period.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Domestic violence statistics are not discussed in the sources opened.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: The sources do not discuss civilizational differences in political institutions.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Berger criticised militarism and relied on elected government, which excludes a political guardian role for the army.

paid-care-work.rationale: Pay for unpaid care work is not covered in the sources opened, so no stance is documented.

filial-duty.rationale: Duties of adult children are not addressed in the sources opened.

office-by-exam.rationale: Hoan created a merit system for police and fire departments, applying exam-style civil service principles.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: The sources give no view on foreign ownership of firms.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Divorce law is not discussed in any source opened.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Not addressed directly; Berger accepted representative parliamentary politics.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Not addressed directly, but Berger as congressman proposed old-age pensions, a public scheme.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Community ownership of land was not a sewer socialist aim; Berger allied with farmers who held their land.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from parliamentary politics.

single-official-language.rationale: The movement's multilingual party press suggests it opposed imposing a single language, but this is inferred.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Not discussed in the sources opened.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Disparate impact doctrine is anachronistic and not covered in sources.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Berger criticised commercialism but not consumerism as such.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Berger's opposition to imperialism and foreign war implies opposition to arming insurgents abroad.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Antiimperialist outlook rejects great powers sending troops into allied countries.

corporate-influence.rationale: Berger said the US had a government of plutocracy and the capitalist class.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: The sources contain nothing on foreign funding of civil society.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Population policy through child bonuses is not discussed in the sources opened.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local limits on property purchases are not addressed in any source opened.

job-guarantee.rationale: Never stated in the sources opened; inferred from the program's emphasis on lifting workers out of poverty and on public works.

democratic-peace.rationale: Berger's sources do not make claims about democracy and war, so there is no stated position.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Berger accepted majority rule and compromise as the basis of politics, which implies a general duty to follow the law; inferred.

non-intervention.rationale: Berger's antiwar and anti-imperial stance implies agreement that states should not intervene in each other's affairs; inferred.

industrial-unions.rationale: Berger defended the AFL against the IWW in 1906 but the sources do not say whether he favored industrial or craft organisation, so adherents are split.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Berger described the war-time hatred suffered by Jews, Irish and others and condemned racial hatred, so conspiracy claims against a minority are rejected.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Abolishing legal marriage is not discussed in the sources, and a reform-minded municipal movement is unlikely to hold it.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The movement's identity rested on exposing graft and demonstrating honest government, so open access to government records fits it; inferred.

local-production.rationale: Local production for local consumption is not discussed; the movement's municipal enterprises were largely utilities and public markets.

informal-organisation.rationale: Berger insisted on an organised electoral party and attacked sectarian and anarchist-style noise, so small informal groups are not the model.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Not discussed in the sources opened.

religious-nation.rationale: A secular, immigrant-based movement rejects defining the nation by shared religion.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Ritual submission to a leading power is the opposite of the anti-imperialist stance Berger took.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: The sources do not discuss regional fiscal sharing.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The program targeted monopolies and utilities rather than personal belongings.

defeat-communism.rationale: Berger fought communists within the party but also condemned the government's red-baiting; split.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: The movement's program was public provision of utilities and services, so a mix with private providers is disfavoured; inferred.

religion-illusion.rationale: Berger sceptical of heavens but the movement avoided religious debate; split.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Berger said a great deal has been done under capitalism and that it will grow into socialism.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Not discussed in the sources opened.

socialized-care.rationale: Municipal child health programs existed, such as medical exams, but housework and childcare as public services are not documented.

purge-loanwords.rationale: The movement ran papers in several immigrant languages and would not purge foreign words.

treaties-binding.rationale: Treaties with nations within borders are not discussed in the sources opened.

cooperative-communities.rationale: The movement's program was municipal administration and national reform, not reorganising society into small cooperative communities.

majority-settlement.rationale: Berger condemned national and racial hatreds, so encouraging settlement to dilute minorities contradicts that.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Berger rejected both Bolshevism and capitalist plutocracy while seeking a democratic socialism; fits partly.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Berger's anti-nationalism opposes land claims based on historical or religious ties; inferred.

holocaust-denial.rationale: The Holocaust postdates the sources, but a movement that condemned the persecution of Jews would reject denial.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: The sources do not discuss sexual law; a progressive reform movement is unlikely to favour criminalising it.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Berger was prosecuted and persecuted for opposition during the war and condemned government terror, so he rejects suppression.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: A secular, free-press movement that suffered censorship rejects blasphemy laws.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Berger's anti-imperialism opposes governing overseas territories for the metropole's benefit.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Not discussed in the sources opened and outside the movement's setting.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: A secular democratic movement rejects removing rulers for not following religious law.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Berger's party stressed elected representatives and parliamentary work, though direct participation is not ruled out; the sources are silent.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: The framework is anachronistic and absent from the movement's sources.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Anachronistic for the period and absent from the sources.

assisted-dying.rationale: Not discussed in any source opened.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Berger insisted on keeping a distinct Socialist identity and never fusing with other groups.

alienated-labor.rationale: Alienation theory does not appear in the sources opened; Berger concentrated on practical reforms.

islam-incompatible.rationale: The sources do not address Islam, but a movement condemning racial and religious hatred would reject this claim.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Berger's secular, parliamentary socialism rests on popular democratic rule and he mocked heavens of every kind.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Inferred from the movement's secular, Turner-influenced outlook; no source discusses religious dress.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Inferred from Berger's labor-legislation agenda; harassment settlements are anachronistic and not addressed.

social-market-economy.rationale: Milwaukee's municipal ownership sat beside private business and sought steady change toward socialism, so adherents are split between a mixed economy and eventual public ownership; inferred.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Berger opposed militarism and favoured an armed people (a citizen militia) but did not call for abolishing all armed forces; inferred.

rich-first.rationale: Inferred: a labor-backed movement aiming to improve workers' lives now would reject leaving some behind for later gains; the sources are silent on staged growth.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Berger opposed US entry into the First World War and entangling commitments, which fits staying out of rival power blocs.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Berger's evolutionary socialism worked inside the democratic republic and wanted extension of democracy, so inherited office is rejected.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Sewer socialists favoured public ownership of utilities and cooperative help, but the sources do not mention user-owned banking; inferred as indifferent.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Hoan stressed fiscal prudence and paying down city debt, but the movement never faced international lenders; adherents are split.

property-franchise.rationale: Berger built a labour-backed party on the vote of the working class, which a property or tax qualification would exclude.

domination-women-nature.rationale: The movement's focus was municipal services; it did not address this linkage.

reification.rationale: Berger preferred concrete reforms and rejected revolutionary theory, so abstract critiques like reification are inferred as alien to it.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Berger's writing attacked plutocracy and the press's role in the war persecution of socialists, which fits the claim.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Hoan's merit system and anti-graft politics stressed honest, rule-bound government.

racial-franchise.rationale: Berger held racist views on some groups, but the party platform stood for the working-class vote; the sources do not show support for a racial franchise.

online-participation.rationale: Internet participation is anachronistic for 1897-1930s; inferred as unaddressed.

open-government-data.rationale: The movement's anti-graft focus implies that city business should be open to inspection, inferred rather than documented.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: A secular, reformist labour party with an immigrant German-Catholic and Jewish base is inferred to oppose marriage restrictions by faith.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Berger criticised national hatreds and the movement organised across ethnic lines in unions; boycotting a religious minority is inferred as opposed.

citizens-assembly.rationale: The movement governed through elected councils and officials; citizens' assemblies are an unaddressed later device.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Religious reform was outside the movement's municipal program; adherents are indifferent.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Berger attacked plutocracy and the power of concentrated capital over working people, which fits the claim.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; inferred neutral.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The movement was pragmatic and focused on municipal services and the ballot, and was not an atheist or anti-religion program; inferred.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Sewer socialists sought honest and efficient municipal government and merit-based public services, not abolition of police.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Not addressed; Milwaukee's problem was a working-class municipal majority, not a divided state.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The movement's signature claim was that publicly owned services run by city hall improve workers' lives, which rejects charity as the main provider.

term-limits.rationale: Not addressed; Hoan held office for decades, but the movement set no principle either way.

vote-delegation.rationale: Not addressed; Berger favoured representative government and the ballot, so no stance on delegation is inferred.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Not addressed by a movement of 1897-1930s municipal reformers.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Not addressed; adherents' views on religious office are unrecorded.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred from the movement's social-democratic equality principles and its support for women's suffrage; marriage was not discussed directly.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from an immigrant-heavy labour base and Berger's opposition to national hatreds.

rent-control.rationale: Not addressed in the period; inferred from a municipal-socialist commitment to public housing and limits on private gain, later seen in Zeidler's housing work.

abolish-ip.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a reformist programme that left private rights over inventions alone.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from its anti-militarist, anti-war stance and hostility to state drilling of youth.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from its opposition to U.S. entry into the First World War and to militarism.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from its anti-war, anti-militarist position.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from Berger's denunciation of national hatreds and persecution.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The party's core claim was that plutocracy and returns on property should give way to the working population; Berger wrote against plutocracy.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Not addressed; Berger spoke for an armed people, so adherents did not take an absolute pacifist line.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Inferred from an internationalist socialism that opposed national hatreds.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Anachronistic; the movement predates such theory and kept to economic reform.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from a class-based politics that did not question the category of women.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred from Berger's opposition to the war and to nationalist fervour.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Inferred from its reformist, materialist working programme, which Berger set against revolutionary phrases and moral crusades.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Anachronistic; the movement took no stance on diaspora and homeland questions.

culture-before-state.rationale: Inferred from the strategy of winning municipal power and building up services for workers.

god-not-male.rationale: The movement was secular and indifferent to religious language.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Anachronistic; the movement took no position on religious texts.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Inferred from Berger's internationalism and opposition to national hatreds, though Berger himself held racist views on race.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from city-based reformism that took no stand on merging regions for a people.

independent-unions.rationale: Milwaukee's socialists were closely allied with the trade unions and worked with, rather than commanded, organised labour.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Berger's party was a working-class party seeking to win power by the ballot for workers; the exact claim in the statement is inferred.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Municipal ownership and honest running of water, sanitation, power and similar services was the movement's signature programme.

second-chamber.rationale: The sources do not discuss legislative structure, and nothing in the programme points either way.

municipal-property.rationale: Municipal ownership of utilities was its practical programme, though the longer-term aim was collective ownership under a democratic state.

confederal-coordination.rationale: The movement stressed city home rule but built no confederal structure; adherents were pragmatic about the form of coordination.

family-wage.rationale: Berger's programme aimed at raising working families' living standards; the family wage itself is inferred.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Not addressed; inferred only that the movement's public health measures were pro-science, which does not settle the question.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Not addressed; anachronistic for the movement.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Not addressed; anachronistic for the movement.

online-anonymity.rationale: Not addressed; anachronistic for the movement.

person-over-state.rationale: Inferred from the movement's democratic, reformist and civil-liberties stance, including opposition to wartime repression; Berger was prosecuted under the Espionage Act.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Not addressed; the movement was secular and practical, and nothing in the sources says whether it saw a spiritual nature as political.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Milwaukee's socialists wanted greater city home rule against state-level limits, so they would not rest self-government on revocable powers; inferred.

gm-crops.rationale: Not addressed; anachronistic for the movement.

dense-cities.rationale: Their reforms included parks and planning for working-class neighbourhoods, but density versus suburb as an environmental claim is anachronistic.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The movement organised on class, not race, and sought a broad workers' coalition; inferred from its class framing.

racial-pride.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; inferred as outside the movement's class-based framework.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Berger and the Milwaukee socialists opposed U.S. entry into the First World War and condemned it as a capitalist war.

missingStatements.text: Water, power and transit utilities should be owned and run by city governments rather than private companies.
missingStatements.rationale: Municipal ownership of utilities was the movement's signature demand and Hoan fought for city ownership of power and streetcars.

missingStatements.text: Public officials should be held to strict honesty, and fighting graft is the first duty of a reforming government.
missingStatements.rationale: Rooting out corruption and showing honest, efficient local government was the movement's central claim and reputation.
missingStatements.declined: Near-universally agreed in principle, so it would not discriminate between ideologies; political-elite-corrupt covers the theme.

missingStatements.text: Socialism should be pursued through the ballot and a program of immediate reforms rather than waiting for a revolution.
missingStatements.rationale: Berger insisted on a working program and steady reform, scorning revolutionary phrases.

notes: Berger held racial and eugenicist views that other Milwaukee socialists, including Frank Zeidler later, did not share, so race-related answers are low confidence. Wartime positions split: Berger was prosecuted for opposing the war while Hoan administered draft registration.
